pr_title: Feature(commit-msg): add canned messages for pre-determined change sets
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 13 of 13 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Every new test is behavioral: real git clones, the real capture/build pipeline and the real lookup, with no mock-chain wiring.
The lookalike parametrization (PR_REVIEWS_old, docs/other, a bare pr_review_agent_usage.json) pins the whole-path versus file-name split in _matches.
test_every_canned_message_passes_the_message_checks runs each LOOKUP entry through message_problems, so a new entry with a malformed header fails at once.
The canned subcommand tests cover argv, stdin, a mixed set and empty input, and assert the exact stdout.
The merge-skill contract parses the documented `canned` command line with the script's own argparse parser, which catches drift between the skill text and the CLI.
_prefilled only fills an empty message, so messages carried forward from an existing TXT or pending TXT are never overwritten.
Both canned subjects ('Chore(todo): ...', 'Chore(reviews): ...') pass _HEADER_RULE and contain no filler or vendor names, so a prefilled skeleton builds without edits.
LOOKUP is wrapped in MappingProxyType with frozenset keys and get_canned_message normalizes backslashes and leading './', so Windows-style and git-style paths match alike.
The `canned` subcommand is wired through the existing parser, the dispatch table and the usage docstring in the same way as the other subcommands.

README Canned commit messages section matches canned_messages.py exactly: the patterns, both messages, the all-files-of-one-entry rule, the slash-means-whole-path matching, and the fallback for projects that moved the defaults.
The 'build still checks it' claim holds: canned messages run through message_problems, and both LOOKUP values pass _HEADER_RULE (Chore is a valid type).
c-msg prose matches pending_document: a pending draft against the same HEAD takes precedence and canned fills only an empty message; 'go to Step 3' points at the real Build step.
tests/skills/test_canned_message_skill_contract.py parses the merge skill's canned command line with the script's real argparse parser, so that doc line cannot drift silently.
_prefilled never overrides a carried message: a pending or branch draft wins over the canned text, and test_a_carried_message_wins_over_the_canned_one pins that.

The canned messages still go through build validation: test_every_canned_message_passes_the_message_checks runs each LOOKUP message through message_problems, and test_a_prefilled_message_builds runs the real build.
The skill contract test parses the merge skill's 'canned' command line with the script's real argparse parser, so prose drift from the CLI fails CI.
The tests are behavioral against real git clones and the real lookup; no test stubs a helper and asserts on the stub.
Matching is precise: patterns with a slash match the whole path, others the file name, and the lookalike-path parametrized test guards against false positives.
The docs land together: README, the script docstring, all four commit-message skills and the plugin version bump move in one change.

important.name: --fresh docstring still promises empty messages
important.summary:
The module docstring says `--fresh` replans from the rules and 'messages come back empty'. After this PR, run_capture passes every fresh group through _prefilled (lines 247-249), so a block covered by a canned set comes back with the canned message even under --fresh. The skill format doc makes the same claim ('every message is empty'), so the documented contract and the code now disagree.

Also (runtime): capture runs the lookup separately for each block (lines 247-249). If planning splits files from one canned set into two blocks (for example, a TODO catalog and a snapshot that land in different buckets), both blocks get the same canned subject. A one-file block also gets a subject that claims more than it changed ('refresh TODO catalog, research stubs and snapshot'). build accepts duplicate subjects, so nothing flags it.

Also (overall): run_capture now passes every planned block through _prefilled, including under --fresh, so a fresh capture returns the canned message for a TODO-only or review-artifact-only block. The script docstring (branch_commit_msg.py:10-11, 'messages come back empty') and the branch-commit-msg skill (SKILL.md:45 table row 'every message ""', SKILL.md:56-57 'every message is ""') still say a fresh capture empties every message. The skill's own new sentence at :54-56 covers only the carry-forward case, so the --fresh rows contradict the code.
fix: Change line 11 to 'messages come back empty, except a block covered by a canned set, which gets its canned message' and make the same edit to txt_format.md line 106.
In run_capture, prefill a canned message for only the first block that matches a given LOOKUP entry and leave later matches empty for drafting.
Have message_problems report two blocks with an identical subject.
Reword branch_commit_msg.py:10-11 to 'messages come back empty, except a canned block (canned_messages)' and SKILL.md:45/:57 to 'every message "" except a canned set's'.

important.name: branch-commit-msg still says --fresh empties every message
important.summary: SKILL.md lines 56-57 keep the pre-PR sentence 'Add `--fresh` to ignore the existing TXT: the plan is rebuilt from the rules alone and every message is `""`.' At the head, run_capture builds every block through _prefilled(group.paths, group.message) (plugins/harness/scripts/branch_commit_msg.py), and --fresh only drops the existing document, so a fresh capture still prefills a canned block's message. The lines just above (54-56) also limit the prefill to 'new blocks', yet _prefilled runs on every group, including a kept block that capture emptied (the Docs/Planning merge). The skill now contradicts itself and the code, and an agent that trusts the --fresh sentence redrafts a canned block.
fix: Change lines 56-57 to: 'Add `--fresh` to ignore the existing TXT: the plan is rebuilt from the rules alone and every message is `""` except a canned block's.' Also reword line 54 from 'new blocks have `""`, except ...' to 'a new or emptied block has `""`, except ...'.

important.name: Subset test passes vacuously when the TODO entry is gone
important.summary: test_a_subset_of_an_entry_takes_its_message asserts get_canned_message(TODO_FILES) == get_canned_message(['RepoToDo.json']). If the TODO entry is dropped or both lookups break, both sides are None and the test still passes. It never checks that the subset actually gets a message, which is the claim in its name.
fix: Assert the subset's message directly: `assert get_canned_message(['RepoToDo.json']) == get_canned_message(TODO_FILES) is not None`, or compare against the literal 'Chore(todo): ...' message.

important.name: Normalization test never reaches a whole-path pattern
important.summary: test_paths_normalize_before_matching uses only TODO files, which match by file name. For a name pattern the leading './' makes no difference, because PurePosixPath(path).name ignores it, so the './docs/TODO/_IMPL_TODO.md' case passes even with no normalization. Only the backslash case can fail. The leading-'./' handling promised by _norm_path matters only for slash patterns such as 'docs/PR_REVIEWS/*.json', and no test feeds one a './' or backslash path. A regression there (for example from `gh pr diff --name-only` output or Windows paths fed to `canned`) goes undetected.
fix: Add whole-path cases: `assert has_canned_message(['./docs/PR_REVIEWS/0001_x.json', 'docs\PR_SUMMARIES\0001_x.md'])`, either in this test or as a parametrized companion.

important.name: No test checks that a carried message beats the canned one in branch capture or amend
important.summary: run_capture now sends every planned block through _prefilled(group.paths, group.message), and amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md promises that a block emptied by a new path 'comes back with the canned message'. TestCannedMessages checks the 'carried wins' precedence only for capture --pending (test_a_carried_message_wins_over_the_canned_one). Neither the branch-capture path (a block carried from an existing TXT) nor the amend path is checked. If the `message or canned` order were swapped in run_capture, drafted branch messages would be overwritten silently and every test would still pass.
fix: Add a branch-mode test: with _settled_with_todo_change, run_capture(base='HEAD'), run_build with _filled(...), capture again, and assert the TODO block keeps 'Chore: commit N...'.
Optionally add an amend-mode test: a block emptied by a new path inside the TODO set comes back holding the canned message.

minor.name: 'default file names and folders' overstates the TODO entry's path dependence
minor.summary: README.md:182 and canned_messages.py:8-9 say that a project which moves the files away from the defaults drafts as usual. The TODO entry's patterns have no '/', so _matches compares only the file name (canned_messages.py:41). Moving the TODO folder (todo.folder, snapshots.dir) keeps the canned message; only renaming the files, or moving the review artifacts, drops it.
fix: README.md:182: 'The entries use the plugin's default file names (and, for review artifacts, folders); a project that renames them drafts as usual.' Mirror the wording in canned_messages.py:8-9.

minor.name: LOOKUP hardcodes paths that already exist as config keys
minor.summary:
LOOKUP spells out values that are already configurable: artifacts.reviews, artifacts.summaries, todo.catalog, todo.stub_name, todo.snapshots.name_pattern, todo.research.catalog, and the basenames of matrix_path and agent_usage_path. The project rule is that library code reads active() inside its functions. As written, a project that overrides any of these keys silently loses the shortcut. The module docstring (lines 8-9) admits the limitation, and tests/lib/test_canned_messages.py pins LOOKUP to the defaults, so this is not a drift bug, but it goes against the plugin's config-driven convention.

Also (overall): LOOKUP hardcodes seven names and paths that the plugin already exposes as config keys: todo.catalog, todo.stub_name, todo.research.catalog, the todo.snapshots name_pattern, artifacts.reviews, artifacts.summaries, matrix_path and agent_usage_path. A project that overrides any of them silently loses the shortcut. The scripts already activate config before calling get_canned_message, so the module could read active() inside the function, as the 'drivers activate, library code reads' rule in CLAUDE.md describes. The test module's autouse _default_project fixture (test_canned_messages.py:28-30) activates a config that the code under test never reads, so it is dead setup. test_the_patterns_cover_the_plugin_defaults (95-103) pins only the defaults and uses a made-up snapshot name instead of todo.snapshots.name_pattern.
fix: Build the pattern sets inside get_canned_message from active() (artifacts.reviews + '/*.json', artifacts.summaries + '/*.md', basenames of matrix_path/agent_usage_path, todo.* names), and keep the fixed messages in a module constant.
Keep the literals but add a note to README/CLAUDE.md that canned sets assume the default artifact and todo names.
Build the entries from active() inside get_canned_message (todo/artifacts/matrix/usage keys), and have the tests activate a project with overridden keys to prove the lookup follows them.
Or keep the hardcoded defaults as an accepted limitation: delete the dead autouse fixture and say in the module docstring why config is not read.

minor.name: 'exactly' in the prefill docs contradicts subset matching
minor.summary: _prefilled's docstring ('a block of exactly ``paths``') and the `canned` section ('a block of exactly the TODO files') say the block must match the canned set exactly. get_canned_message uses subset semantics (canned_messages.py lines 3-5, 45-47): a block holding only RepoToDo.json, or only pr_review_agent_usage.jsonl, also qualifies. The skill docs correctly say 'holding only the files of a canned set'.
fix: Change both to 'a block whose every path falls in a canned set' (line 53: 'a block of only TODO files, say').

minor.name: `canned` with no args blocks on an interactive stdin
minor.summary: _cmd_canned reads sys.stdin whenever no paths are given. Run by hand with no paths, the command hangs until EOF instead of saying input is required. It also calls activate_project, so it needs a git checkout with a valid config even though it reads no config.
fix: When `not args.paths and sys.stdin.isatty()`, raise BuildError(['canned: give paths as arguments or pipe one per line on stdin']).

minor.name: amend-commit-msg canned paragraph breaks the 'emptied this way' antecedent and conflicts with the touched-block rule
minor.summary:
The new paragraph at lines 54-55 sits between the bullet list of ways capture empties a block (48-52) and 'A block emptied this way counts as touched ... restate it in Step 4 with a bullet for the new path' (57-59). 'This way' now reads as if it refers to the canned prefill. The two rules also collide: a Docs block of only TODO files that gains a new snapshot is emptied by capture, then refilled by _prefilled with the canned text. Lines 54-55 say keep it as it stands, while 57-59 and Step 4 (line 102, one bullet for every non-artifact path; the TODO files are not Artifact-bucket) say to restate it with bullets. The old TXT message, even one the developer edited, is dropped silently. README.md line 180 repeats the 'keep as it stands' half.

Also (overall): In amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md the new canned paragraph (54-55) sits between the bullet list that defines how a block gets emptied (48-52) and the paragraph that starts 'A block emptied this way counts as touched' (57-59). 'This way' now reads as if it refers to the canned prefill, which tells the agent to restate an old message for a block the line above says to keep as it stands.
fix: Move lines 54-55 below the 'A block emptied this way counts as touched' paragraph and say a canned block is the exception: 'Exception: a block holding only the files of a canned set (...) comes back with the canned message instead of an empty one; it is not touched, so keep it as it stands and add no bullets.'
Move the canned paragraph (54-55) below the 'A block emptied this way...' paragraph (after line 59).

minor.name: merge-commit-msg puts a conventional-commit subject in the prose slot
minor.summary: Line 46 says the canned message 'replaces the drafted prose paragraph, as it stands'. Every LOOKUP value is a '<Type>(<scope>): <subject>' header (for example 'Chore(todo): refresh TODO catalog, research stubs and snapshot'), so the merge body gets a second subject line under 'Merge PR #NNN — <title>' where the Output Shape template (lines 76-80) asks for lead-with-the-action prose. Nothing breaks, but the result does not match the documented shape, and the haiku-run skill gets no guidance on whether to strip the 'Chore(...):' prefix.
fix: State the intended rendering explicitly, for example 'use the printed message as the prose paragraph verbatim, Type(scope) prefix included'.
Or drop the 'Type(scope): ' prefix and capitalize the rest, for example 'Refresh TODO catalog, research stubs and snapshot.'

minor.name: Defaults-coverage test hard-codes the snapshot name its docstring says it derives
minor.summary: The docstring says 'A default path or name changed in defaults.json must change the entry that names it', but the snapshot is the literal 'TODO_Snapshot_2026_1023.md' and is not built from todo.snapshots.name_pattern. If that default changes, for example to a different prefix or a .json suffix, the test still passes while capture stops prefilling snapshots.
fix: Build the sample snapshot name from defaults['todo']['snapshots']['name_pattern'], for example by substituting a date into the named group and checking that re.fullmatch accepts it, then assert has_canned_message on that name.
At minimum, assert that the name_pattern starts with 'TODO_Snapshot_' and ends with '\.md' so a change to the default fails here.

minor.name: Skill contract leaves amend-commit-msg out of the 'keep it' check its docstring claims
minor.summary:
The module docstring says the test pins 'that each skill says what to do with a prefilled message'. test_a_prefilled_block_is_not_redrafted, however, is parametrized over only c-msg and branch-commit-msg. amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md now says 'keep it as it stands' about the canned block, and nothing pins that sentence.

Also (tests): In test_capture_skills_keep_a_canned_message, `'canned' in body` is implied by the next assertion, `'canned_messages.py' in body`, so the first can never fail on its own.
fix: Parametrize test_a_prefilled_block_is_not_redrafted over _CAPTURE_SKILLS.
Drop the first assertion, or make it check something distinct, such as a 'canned message' phrase outside the module path.
